newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAG union says no to more austerity.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAG union says no to more austerity.

text.p: The top official of the DAG white-collar trade union said on Sunday the German union would reject any further austerity measures by Bonn in its bid to whip Germany's finances into shape for European currency union.
DAG leader Roland Issen said additional cost-cutting measures would only harm Germany's near-record unemployment situation and fail to help create new jobs.

But Issen said he was still in favour of the planned single European currency, dubbed the euro and set for launch in January 1999, saying the advantages for export-sensitive Germany would outweigh the disadvantages.
Issen's comments came after German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said at the weekend in an interview with Focus magazine that he could not rule out further austerity measures.
Many economists expect Germany to fail in 1997 to meet the budget deficit limit of three percent of Gross Domestic Product needed to join currency union as outlined in the Maastricht Treaty.
Bonn has rejected the predictions, saying it still believed it could meet the entry criteria in 1997, the year whose economic data will be critical for membership selection.
